  • Vanguard Adviser's Alpha (UK edition) — Quantifies specific behaviours adding ~3% per year in value
  • Morningstar Mind the Gap 2025 — Persistent 1.2% annual shortfall between fund returns and investor returns
  • ILC–Royal London: "What It's Worth" (2019) — £47,706 wealth uplift over a decade for those who received advice
  • Royal London: "Feeling the Benefit of Financial Advice" — 4,000+ UK customers on the emotional and wellbeing impact of advice
  • MacDonald et al. (2023) — Accounting & Finance — Academic systematic review covering the full evidence base across financial and non-financial value dimensions
Chapter 8

Common mistakes people make when starting the process

Before you even get to choosing an adviser, there are a number of common mistakes that can make the financial planning process slower, more stressful, or more expensive than it needs to be.

❌ Avoid

Approaching advice without clear goals or priorities — expecting an adviser to define your objectives for you

✓ Do instead

Spend time reflecting on what you want your future to look like. As Seneca said: "If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable."

❌ Avoid

Jumping straight to "which product is best?" Products are tools — they come after design, not before

✓ Do instead

Start with life planning, strategy, and priorities before thinking about structures like ISAs, pensions, or portfolios

❌ Avoid

Handing over partial or outdated information — missing documents slow everything down and increase the risk of unsuitable advice

✓ Do instead

Gather complete, current records before the planning process begins

❌ Avoid

Thinking a financial plan is something you "complete" — a single meeting or report

✓ Do instead

View planning as ongoing maintenance — the way a garden stays healthy over time. Your world changes; your plan must too

❌ Avoid

Focusing only on investments and pensions while excluding property, business interests, cash reserves, and family commitments

✓ Do instead

Prepare to discuss your whole financial world. Planning is interconnected — missing pieces distort the outcome

❌ Avoid

Treating financial planning as purely technical — ignoring how you actually react to volatility, risk, and stress

✓ Do instead

Be open about your behaviours, fears, and preferences. Advice is not just numbers

Chapter 9

Finding the right guide

A financial adviser isn't just someone who sets up accounts or builds portfolios. They're someone you trust with decisions that affect your children, your future stability, and your long-term wellbeing. The right guide shows their quality through their behaviour, not their promises.

"Trust doesn't come from confidence. It comes from clarity, competence, and honesty."Dominic Baldwin, Founder — Xentum, on choosing his daughter's surgeon and what it taught him about choosing any professional

Seven signs you've found the right adviser

1. They start with you, not themselves
They begin by understanding your life, goals, concerns, and values — not your products or portfolio. The wrong adviser jumps straight to solutions. The right adviser builds understanding before offering any.
2. They are transparent, even when it's uncomfortable
They explain the limits of what they can do, the risks, the trade-offs, the full cost, and the reasoning behind recommendations. No spin. No jargon. No gloss.
3. They listen more than they talk
Good advisers ask thoughtful questions. Great advisers ask better questions than you expected. If you leave the first meeting feeling truly heard, that's a strong signal.
4. They demonstrate their process clearly
You shouldn't have to guess how they work, how often you'll review things, or what happens when your circumstances change. If they can't articulate their process simply, the process probably doesn't exist.
5. They avoid predictions and promises
They won't claim to beat the market, avoid downturns, or guarantee outcomes. They focus on what can be controlled — discipline, structure, behaviour, tax efficiency, and long-term alignment.
6. They talk about your life, not their products
The right adviser talks about your future, your fears, your family, your options, your decisions, and your purpose. Financial planning is about life first, money second.
7. They are happy to say "we're not the right fit"
The wrong adviser tries to win every client. The right adviser only works with clients they can genuinely help. If an adviser recommends a different firm because they believe it's better for you, that is one of the strongest marks of integrity.

Practical checks before choosing

  • Are they regulated? Check the FCA register at register.fca.org.uk before you do anything else
  • Are they independent or restricted — and can they clearly explain why that's right for you?
  • What do their existing clients say — on VouchedFor, Google, or Unbiased?
  • Can they clearly explain their full fee structure, including all external costs?
  • Do they have a specialist planning process, or do they primarily sell and manage investments?
  • Are they willing to refer you elsewhere if they're not the right fit?
  • Do they work with specialists — accountants, solicitors — and can they explain how?

How we think about fees

Our fee model. Why it exists. What it isn't.

We charge fixed and tiered fees. Not because fixed fees are inherently superior to percentage-based fees — they aren't — but because they represent a genuine structural alternative that works well for the clients we serve.

The honest picture is more nuanced than most firms admit. Part of the value of financial advice is proportionate to the assets involved. Part isn't. Understanding both is essential to understanding why we charge the way we do.

We are not the cheapest option. We are a high-quality alternative with a different, more transparent pricing structure. Chartered Financial Planners, independent, using the best available technology. The service justifies the fee.

Why fixed fees — honestly
✓Cost certainty. You know what you'll pay, year on year. Our fees rise with CPI — not with market returns.
✓Reduced conflicts of interest. We earn the same whether your portfolio grows or shrinks. Read how we manage conflicts →
✓Complexity-based pricing. Fees reflect the work involved — not the number on your investment statement.
→It's not always cheaper. At lower asset levels, a fixed fee can be higher than 0.5% AUM. We're transparent about this — and we're comfortable targeting the clients where our model is genuinely better value.
The proportionate case — what the evidence says

Vanguard's Adviser's Alpha research — one of the most cited studies in financial planning — quantifies the value a good adviser adds. The study identifies specific adviser behaviours that together add up to approximately 3% per year in net value. These include:

Investor coaching
1.5%
Preventing emotional decisions during market falls — the largest single driver of adviser value
Tax & withdrawal strategy
1.1%
Asset location, tax wrapper use, and sustainable withdrawal sequencing combined
Portfolio rebalancing
0.48%
Systematic rebalancing versus letting drift affect risk exposure over time
Low-cost investing
0.44%
Selecting cost-efficient funds and platforms that compound favourably over decades

The proportionate point: These benefits are largely proportionate to the portfolio they're applied to. Behavioural coaching that prevents a 10% panic-sell on a £2m portfolio saves £200,000. The same coaching on a £100k portfolio saves £10,000. This is why a proportion of adviser value genuinely does scale with assets — and why a percentage model isn't entirely without logic.

But the intangible value doesn't scale: Peace of mind, clarity about big decisions, confidence in retirement, fewer arguments about money — these are equally valuable whether your portfolio is £500k or £5m. A fee structure that charges purely on assets captures one dimension of value and ignores the other entirely.

Starts with your life, not your investments. Discovery conversations focus on your goals, values, and priorities — not products. Money is the tool; your life is the plan. We use our Grab Life Wheel → to help clients articulate what really matters before any financial conversation begins.

Vanguard: Quantifying the Adviser's Alpha in the UK (2024). Read the research →
The proportionate value

Behavioural coaching, tax structuring, rebalancing discipline, withdrawal strategy. Each of these benefits scales with the portfolio they're applied to. Vanguard puts this at ~3% per year in net value.

The intangible value

63% of advised clients feel financially secure vs 48% without advice (Royal London). Advised clients are less anxious, sleep better, make better decisions. These benefits don't scale with portfolio size.

Our position

A fee based purely on assets captures one dimension and ignores the other. Our model prices the work — with a tier structure that rises with complexity, not market returns. For the clients we serve, this is a fairer and more transparent structure.

What we are — and aren't

We are Chartered Financial Planners — a status held by fewer than 15% of UK advice firms. We work independently across the whole market. We use Voyant for cashflow modelling and hold our advisers to standards that the best firms in the country would recognise. We are not cheap. We are not positioning ourselves as a low-cost disruptor. We are a high-quality financial planning firm with a pricing structure that is transparent, complexity-based, and aligned with the interests of the clients we serve.

Implementation Guide
What will I need to set up?
Fee calculator guide

What will I need to set up?
A plain-English guide to every implementation option

5 min read — written to help you fill in the fee calculator accurately

Most people sit down with the fee calculator and hit a wall at Section 4 — "what do you need us to set up?" This guide walks through every option in plain English: what it is, who typically needs it, and how to know whether it applies to you.

You don't need to know exactly what you need — that's partly what the planning process is for. If you're genuinely unsure about something, tick it anyway and we'll work it out together in your first conversation. Also worth knowing: we automatically identify your main piece of work (the most complex item) and list everything else as additional. Adding more items doesn't always raise the fee proportionally — the tier cap and complexity discount apply to the total.

Investments & ISAs

Straightforward

Opening a new ISA

A tax-free wrapper for your savings or investments. Any growth, dividends, or interest inside it is completely free of tax, forever. You can put in up to £20,000 per tax year per person.

Tick this if
You have cash or investments you'd like to shelter from tax
You haven't used your ISA allowance this year
You and a partner both want one — set the count to 2
Skip this if
You already have an ISA and just want it managed — include it in Section 5 instead
You're only transferring — use the transfer option below
Straightforward

Opening a general investment account (GIA)

A flexible investment account with no annual limit and no restrictions on withdrawals. It's taxable — but there's an annual capital gains allowance, and we'll structure withdrawals to use it as efficiently as possible.

Tick this if
You've used your ISA allowance and have more to invest
You're investing a large lump sum and need to drip-feed into ISAs over time
Skip this if
You haven't maxed your ISA yet — put money there first, it's more tax-efficient
Straightforward

Junior ISA or Junior pension (for a child or grandchild)

A Junior ISA lets a child access money at 18. A Junior pension (Junior SIPP) locks money away until age 57 — but you get 20% tax relief on contributions right now, making it a powerful long-term gift.

Tick this if
You want to put money away for a child or grandchild
You'd like to help a child start building long-term wealth early
Set the count to the number of children
Skip this if
The child already has an account — include it in Section 5 instead
Straightforward

Setting up an investment bond

An insurance-based investment wrapper — not a savings bond. It lets you take up to 5% of your original investment each year as income without an immediate tax charge, making it useful for tax-efficient regular withdrawals and estate planning.

Tick this if
You want to take a regular income in a tax-efficient way
Inheritance tax planning is part of what you want to address
You're a higher-rate taxpayer with a large lump sum to invest
Skip this if
You're a basic-rate taxpayer — an ISA or GIA will usually be simpler and just as effective
Straightforward

New ISA / New ISA with transfer(s) in

A tax-free wrapper for your savings or investments. Any growth, dividends, or interest inside it is completely free of tax, forever. You can put in up to £20,000 per tax year per person.

If you have existing ISAs or investments sitting elsewhere, we can open the new ISA and transfer them in as part of the same piece of work. Select New ISA with transfer(s) in and use the How many transfers in? counter to tell us how many separate policies you want to consolidate — each one involves its own research and admin. The cost is slightly higher than a plain new ISA to reflect that extra work, but it's still all one report.

New ISA — tick if
You want to open a fresh ISA with new money only
You and a partner both want one — set the account count to 2
New ISA with transfer(s) in — tick if
You want a new ISA and want to bring one or more existing policies across at the same time
Use the transfers-in counter to set how many policies you're transferring
Straightforward

New GIA / New GIA with transfer(s) in

A flexible investment account with no annual limit and no restrictions on withdrawals. It's taxable — but there's an annual capital gains allowance, and we'll structure withdrawals to use it efficiently. Same transfer(s) in logic as the ISA above applies — use the transfers-in counter to set how many policies you're consolidating.

New GIA — tick if
You've used your ISA allowance and have more to invest with new money
New GIA with transfer(s) in — tick if
You want a new GIA and want to consolidate one or more existing investment accounts at the same time
Skip this if
You haven't maxed your ISA yet — put money there first, it's more tax-efficient
Straightforward

Junior ISA or Junior pension / with transfer(s) in

A Junior ISA lets a child access money at 18. A Junior pension (Junior SIPP) locks money away until age 57 — but you get 20% tax relief on contributions right now. Same transfer-in logic applies if there's an existing junior account to consolidate.

Tick this if
You want to put money away for a child or grandchild
Set the count to the number of children
Skip this if
The child already has an account and you just want it managed ongoing — include it in Section 5
Straightforward

Transfer into an existing account (non-pension)

If you already have an ISA, GIA, or other investment account set up with us — or one is being set up as a separate item in this work — and you want to transfer another existing policy into it, this is the option to use. There's no new account being opened here; it's purely the research and admin involved in transferring an existing policy in.

Tick this if
You have an existing account (already set up or being set up) and want to consolidate additional old policies into it
Set the count to the number of separate transfers — each one is priced separately as the research and admin applies per policy
Don't use this if
You're opening a new account and transferring in at the same time — use the relevant "with transfer(s) in" option above instead
Straightforward

Investment bond

An insurance-based investment wrapper — not a savings bond. It lets you take up to 5% of your original investment each year as income without an immediate tax charge, making it useful for tax-efficient regular withdrawals and estate planning. Slightly more involved than a straightforward ISA or GIA given the additional technical work required.

Tick this if
You want to take a regular income in a tax-efficient way
Inheritance tax planning is part of what you want to address
You're a higher-rate taxpayer with a large lump sum to invest
Skip this if
You're a basic-rate taxpayer — an ISA or GIA will usually be simpler and just as effective
Straightforward

Fund switch within an existing account

If you have an existing investment account, ISA, or pension that's already on a platform but invested in the wrong funds — perhaps a legacy default fund or something no longer aligned to your goals — we can switch it into the right strategy. This doesn't involve opening a new account or transferring to a new provider.

Tick this if
You have an existing account that needs reinvesting into a different strategy
You want to move out of a default fund you were auto-enrolled into
Skip this if
You need to move to a different platform entirely — that's a transfer, use the option above

Pensions

Straightforward

New personal pension (SIPP) / New SIPP with transfer(s) in

A self-invested personal pension you control. The government adds 20% tax relief on contributions — higher-rate taxpayers can claim back more through their tax return. Contributions can come from you personally or your company.

If you also want to bring existing pensions across into the new SIPP, select New SIPP with transfer(s) in and use the How many transfers in? counter to tell us how many pension schemes you want to consolidate. Pension transfers involve more work than investment transfers — there's a statutory process, additional regulatory requirements, and careful suitability analysis per scheme — which is reflected in the higher cost compared to a new SIPP alone.

New SIPP — tick if
You want to open a new pension with new contributions only
You're self-employed and don't have a workplace pension
New SIPP with transfer(s) in — tick if
You want a new pension and want to transfer one or more existing pensions into it at the same time
Use the transfers-in counter to tell us how many pension schemes you're consolidating
Moderate

Transfer into an existing pension

If you already have a pension set up with us — or one is being set up as a separate item in this work — and you want to transfer additional old pensions into it, this covers the research and admin for each additional transfer. There's no new pension being opened; it's the transfer work only.

Tick this if
You have multiple old pensions to consolidate into an existing or newly set-up pension
Set the count to the number of additional pension transfers
Don't use this if
You're opening a new pension and transferring in at the same time — use "New SIPP with transfer(s) in" above
Your pension has guaranteed benefits (final salary) — use the option below
Complex

Transferring a pension with a guarantee (final salary / defined benefit)

Final salary pensions promise a guaranteed income in retirement — usually a proportion of your salary, for life. Transferring means giving up that guarantee in exchange for a lump sum. This is one of the most significant financial decisions a person can make, and we treat it with appropriate care. We won't recommend a transfer unless it's clearly in your interest.

This applies if
You have a final salary pension from a previous employer
You've received a transfer value (CETV) and want to explore whether it makes sense
Probably doesn't apply if
Your pension is from a modern workplace scheme without a guaranteed income promise
Moderate

Taking your first tax free cash payment from your pension

When you first access your pension, you're typically entitled to take up to 25% of the fund as a tax-free lump sum. This is a one-off event and one of the most important decisions in the run-up to retirement — getting the timing and structure right can make a significant difference to your lifetime tax position. We'll model this carefully using your cashflow plan before making any recommendation.

Tick this if
You've reached pension access age (currently 55, rising to 57 in 2028) and want to take your tax-free cash
You're planning to crystallise your pension benefits for the first time
You want to move into drawdown alongside taking your tax-free cash
Skip this if
You've already crystallised your pension and taken your tax-free cash previously
You're many years from retirement and just want to grow your pension
Moderate

Buying an annuity

An annuity converts your pension pot into a guaranteed income — typically for life. You give up flexibility in exchange for certainty. Annuity rates vary significantly between providers, and the difference between a good and average rate can be worth tens of thousands of pounds over a lifetime.

Tick this if
You want certainty over income in retirement above everything else
You're in poor health — you may qualify for an enhanced annuity rate
Skip this if
You want flexibility to take more or less in different years
You have significant guaranteed income already (state pension, final salary)

Protection

Moderate

Personal life cover or income protection

If you died or couldn't work due to illness or injury, would your family be financially secure? This includes life insurance, critical illness cover, and income protection — arranged in your own name.

A note on how we charge for protection: Life cover and income protection are the one area where we receive commission from the insurer rather than charging you a fee. We do this because we want everyone to have appropriate cover — and a fixed advice fee can make smaller policies feel prohibitively expensive, which means people go without. We recognise this creates a conflict of interest. Read how we manage it →
Tick this if
You have dependants who rely on your income
You have a mortgage that couldn't be paid without your income
You're self-employed with no employer sick pay
You haven't reviewed your cover in the last 3 years
Skip this if
You've recently reviewed and are confident your cover is adequate
Moderate

Business protection

If a key director or shareholder died or became seriously ill, what would happen to the business? Business protection covers key person insurance, shareholder protection, and relevant life cover — a tax-efficient way for a company to provide death benefits for a director.

Tick this if
You're a business owner or company director
Your business would be at risk if you or a co-director couldn't work
You have a business partner with no shareholder protection agreement
Skip this if
You're employed rather than a director or owner — personal protection is more relevant

Specialist

Complex

SSAS (small self-administered pension scheme)

A bespoke occupational pension for company directors. Unlike a standard SIPP, a SSAS can lend money back to the sponsoring company, purchase commercial property (including your own business premises), and is more flexible in how it's invested. It comes with significant complexity and ongoing obligations.

Relevant if
You're a director who wants to hold commercial property inside a pension
You want to lend money from your pension to your business
Probably not relevant if
You want a straightforward personal pension — a SIPP will do the job more simply
Complex

VCT (Venture Capital Trust)

A VCT is a listed company that invests in smaller, early-stage UK businesses. Investing in a VCT offers up to 30% income tax relief on the amount invested, tax-free dividends, and no capital gains tax on disposal — in exchange for taking on higher investment risk and committing for at least five years.

Relevant if
You have a significant income tax bill you'd like to reduce
You're comfortable with higher risk and a five-year minimum hold
You've already maximised pension and ISA allowances
Not relevant if
You want stable, accessible investments
You may need the money within five years
Complex

EIS (Enterprise Investment Scheme)

EIS allows you to invest directly in qualifying smaller UK companies and claim up to 30% income tax relief, plus defer capital gains tax and eliminate inheritance tax after a two-year hold. The risk is higher than mainstream investments — you're investing in early-stage businesses — but the tax advantages can be significant for the right client.

Relevant if
You have a large income tax or CGT liability to manage
Inheritance tax planning is a priority
You're a higher or additional rate taxpayer comfortable with illiquid investments
Not relevant if
You want low-risk or easily accessible investments
You might need the capital within three years
Complex

Business Relief investment

Business Relief (BR) investments qualify for 100% inheritance tax relief after a two-year hold, making them a powerful IHT planning tool — particularly for clients who want to retain access to their capital (unlike a gift or trust). They invest in unlisted or AIM-listed businesses and carry more risk than mainstream investments.

Relevant if
Inheritance tax mitigation is a priority and you want to keep access to the money
You've considered or exhausted other IHT options (gifts, trusts, pension)
You're comfortable with the underlying investment risk
Not relevant if
You want low-risk capital preservation
You don't have a meaningful IHT exposure

If you're still unsure after reading this, tick what seems relevant and we'll refine it in your first conversation. Nothing is binding at this stage — the calculator is just to give us both a realistic starting point.

Straightforward pricing.

Why we built this

A little while ago, a business owner got in touch with us. She was approaching a significant exit and needed a financial planner she could trust. We had a good conversation. We genuinely liked her and she said how much she'd enjoyed the meeting. And then she chose someone else.

But she took the time to tell us why — and it was one of the most useful pieces of feedback we've ever received.

She said our fixed fee model was hard to compare. The other firm she was considering charged a percentage of her money — so if she had £5m to invest, she could do the maths herself in seconds. With us, she had no idea what she'd be paying until we'd actually sat down and worked through her situation together. It felt like a leap of faith she wasn't willing to take before she'd even decided whether we were the right fit.

She was right. And she didn't have to tell us — but she did.

So we built this. A straightforward way to work out what you'd pay — before you've spoken to anyone, without any obligation, and in enough detail that you can use it to compare us against any other firm you're considering. That's what this page is for.

How our fees are structured

We charge in two ways: an upfront fee for the work we do to get you set up, and an ongoing annual fee for the advice and service we provide year after year.

What we don't charge for is worth knowing too. We don't charge for investment management, fund switches, top-ups to existing plans, or regular withdrawals. Many advice firms charge for all of these.

Section 2 — WealthPlan
Are you starting with a WealthPlan?
WealthPlan is our financial planning process — the starting point for most new client relationships. It's a structured, collaborative exercise that builds a clear picture of where you are now, where you want to get to, and exactly how your money will get you there. It costs £2,495 and typically takes 6–8 weeks from first meeting to written strategy.

Think of WealthPlan like a thorough health check combined with a roadmap. Before we make a single recommendation, we need to understand the full picture — your financial life today, the goals and the worries, what you've got, what you owe, and what you actually want your money to do for you.

Step 1 — Initial meeting

We get to know each other. You tell us what's brought you here and what you're hoping to achieve. No paperwork, no forms — just a conversation. This is where we decide whether we're a good fit for each other.

Step 2 — Discovery meeting

A deeper conversation about your goals, your priorities, and what financial freedom actually looks like for you. We'll challenge you (gently), gather the facts we need, and start to map out the opportunities and risks in your current situation.

Step 3 — Building your financial strategy

We build a detailed model of your financial future using Voyant — the leading cashflow planning tool used by the UK's top financial planners. We test different scenarios: what if you retire at 55? What if markets fall? What if you stop working for two years? You see the numbers before you make any decisions.

Step 4 — Your written WealthPlan

We produce a clear, written financial plan that includes your family balance sheet, cashflow projections, scenario modelling, tax planning opportunities, and a prioritised action list. Not a brochure — a real working document that guides every decision we make together going forward.

What's included in the annual ongoing fee after WealthPlan is complete: Once your WealthPlan exists, keeping it current is part of your ongoing annual service — at no extra charge. That means annual reviews of your cashflow model, updated projections as your life changes, regular tax planning, and ongoing refinement of the strategy. The plan doesn't sit in a drawer — it's a living document we work from throughout the relationship.

What WealthPlan™ means at Xentum

WealthPlan™ is the combination of Stage 1 (your financial strategy) and Stage 2 (the regulated advice and implementation) — built and delivered as one joined-up process. We start with the Strategy Stage: understanding your life, building your cashflow model, and producing a written financial strategy. Then we move directly into Stage 2: the regulated advice and product setup that turns your strategy into reality. The ongoing relationship that follows is effectively an annual WealthPlan™ — your strategy and implementation revisited together each year as your life evolves.

What WealthPlan™ delivers

Clarity. Strategy. Freedom from guesswork.

How much is enough?

Absolute clarity on the number that gives you freedom — what you need to spend, save, and invest to support the life you want now and in the future.

A strategy you can follow

A prioritised action list — not a brochure. Tax planning, pension structuring, investment strategy, protection — all joined up and written in plain English.

Confidence in every decision

The freedom to use your money without hesitation, knowing the plan has been stress-tested against the scenarios that worry you most.

The WealthPlan™ process

Four meetings. Your written strategy.
Then the advice to action it.

1
Initial meeting · No charge

Is this the right fit?

A conversation — in person, online, or on the phone. Before the Strategy Stage begins, we want to understand whether we're the right long-term partner for you, not just whether building a strategy is the right solution. We'll listen to what's brought you here, explain how we work, and be honest about whether Xentum is the right home for your financial life. No charge, no paperwork, no pressure.

Typically 45–60 minutes
2
Discovery · The Grab Life Wheel

Understanding your life first

Before we touch any financial data, we explore what you actually want. Using our Grab Life Wheel →, we help you identify what matters most, where you're currently happy, and what you want your life to look like. For couples, the results are often illuminating — and the conversation that follows is usually one of the most valuable they've had.

We also research your existing financial arrangements — pensions, investments, protection, property — so we build on what's already in place.

Typically 90 minutes
3
Strategy Stage · Cashflow modelling

Building and testing your plan

We build a detailed cashflow model of your financial life — from today to your 90s. Using Voyant, we stress-test it against the scenarios that worry you most: retiring early, market falls, big spending years, long-term care, inheritance decisions. You see the numbers before any decisions are made.

This is an interactive session — we adjust assumptions in real time and model different strategies together. You leave with a clear sense of what your plan can support and what it can't.

Typically 90 minutes · Most clients say this is where it clicks
4
Strategy Stage deliverable · £2,495

Your written financial strategy

Your strategy document covers your full balance sheet, cashflow projections, tax planning opportunities, investment strategy, protection gaps, and a prioritised action list. This is Stage 1 — the foundation of your WealthPlan™. From here, we move to Stage 2: the regulated advice and implementation that turns strategy into action. Most clients are with us for decades. This is where it starts.

Delivered within 6–8 weeks of your first meeting
Lifetime cashflow modelling

See your future.
Change it if you don't like it.

We use Voyant — one of the leading cashflow modelling platforms in UK financial planning — to build a detailed picture of your financial life over time. It updates in real time, models multiple scenarios simultaneously, and gives you a clear visual representation of what happens if circumstances change.

Seeing your finances mapped across 30–40 years changes how people think about money. It turns abstract fears ("will we run out?") into specific, answerable questions — and specific questions have specific answers.

Xentum Sport · FAQs

Your questions,
answered honestly.

Everything professional athletes and their families ask us before getting started. If your question isn't here, just ask.

Getting started
Do I need a certain amount of money or earnings to work with Xentum Sport?
No minimum earnings threshold. We work with athletes at different stages — from young professionals on their first significant contract to those with established wealth approaching or past the end of their career. What matters is that you're ready to put a proper plan in place, not the size of your contract.
How is Xentum Sport different from a regular financial adviser?
Most financial advisers serve a broad range of clients and have limited experience of the specific pressures athletes face: short career windows, irregular income, tax on image rights and bonuses, agent relationships, and the psychological challenge of life after sport. We've built a service specifically for this context. Our fee model is also fixed — not a percentage of what you have. That means our advice is focused on what's right for you, not on managing as much of your money as possible.
What does a first conversation look like?
It's a straightforward call — usually 30–45 minutes. We listen to where you are, what you're trying to sort out, and whether we're the right fit. There's no charge, no paperwork, and no obligation to proceed. If we're not the right option for you, we'll say so and point you in the right direction.
Can my agent or parent join the conversation?
Yes — we're used to working with families of young professionals and are happy to include agents or parents where that's helpful. That said, the financial plan is always built around you and what you need — not around what's most convenient for the people around you.
Fees and how we charge
Why do you charge a fixed fee instead of a percentage of what I have?
Because a percentage model creates an incentive to manage as much of your money as possible — not to give you the best advice. If we charge 1% of £3m, we earn £30,000 per year whether we do good work or not. A fixed fee means we earn what we charge regardless of your portfolio size. It also gives you cost certainty, which matters when you're planning for a career that has a defined endpoint. As Chris Smalling put it: knowing your adviser isn't taking a percentage of your future gives you real confidence that they're working for you.
How much does it cost?
Our WealthPlan™ is £2,495. Our ongoing service starts from £3,000 per year depending on the complexity of your situation. The full pricing calculator — which shows exactly what you'd pay before any conversation — is on the fees page. See the pricing calculator →
Do you charge separately for investment management?
No. Our ongoing annual fee covers investment management — we don't add a separate layer of charges for managing your portfolio. You'll pay platform fees (charged directly by the platform, not by us) and fund management charges (built into the fund price), but no additional Xentum investment management fee on top of your annual advice fee.
Financial planning for athletes
When is the right time to start financial planning in my career?
As early as possible. The most valuable financial decisions happen at the start of a career — when you first have significant earnings, when you make your first property purchase, when you structure your tax affairs. Athletes who wait until they're 30 to engage a financial planner have typically missed several of the highest-leverage moments. The compounding effect of good early decisions is significant.
What happens to my money when my career ends?
That's exactly what we plan for. Your WealthPlan™ models your entire financial life — not just your playing years. We'll look at how much you need to have accumulated by the time your career ends to support the life you want beyond sport, what passive income your investments can generate, how your property fits into that picture, and what your pension looks like. Life after sport is the goal. We help you build towards it from day one.
Can you help with image rights and tax planning?
Yes — athletes often have complex tax situations involving image rights companies, multiple income streams, and offshore considerations. We work with specialist tax advisers and accountants in this area to ensure your planning is coordinated. We won't give you specific tax advice beyond our regulated remit — that's the accountant's job — but we'll make sure the right professionals are involved and that your financial plan accounts for the tax picture properly.
Do you work with family members too?
Yes. Many of our athlete clients involve family members in their planning — whether that's a partner, parents who have helped with early financial decisions, or siblings. We're comfortable working across a family context where that's helpful. Our starting point is always the athlete's own financial plan, but we can extend planning to family members where needed.

Xentum Family · FAQs

Questions from
families like yours.

The most common questions we hear from individuals and families before they start a WealthPlan™. Honest answers, no jargon.

Getting started
How do I know if I need a financial planner?
A useful test: do you know whether your current financial arrangements will support the life you want in retirement? Do you know whether you could retire earlier than planned? Do you have a clear view of your inheritance tax exposure? If any of these feel uncertain, a financial planner adds real value. Most people don't need a financial planner for simple situations — but most people's situations are more complex than they realise, particularly when property, multiple pensions, children, and estate planning are all in the mix.
What's the minimum amount of money you need to work with Xentum?
We don't have a hard minimum, but our fixed fee structure means we're typically better value for clients with investable assets above £150,000. Below that level, a percentage-based adviser may actually be cheaper — and we'll tell you that honestly if it applies to you. We'd rather not take on clients where we're not the most cost-effective option.
Can couples do a WealthPlan™ together?
Yes — in fact, we strongly encourage it. One of the most valuable parts of the WealthPlan™ process is the Grab Life Wheel, where both partners complete the exercise independently. The results are almost always different, and the conversation that follows — about what each person actually wants from life — is frequently one of the most useful conversations couples have had in years. Financial planning works far better when both people are involved.
I already have a financial adviser. How do I know if I should switch?
Three questions worth asking your current adviser: Can you show me a cashflow model of my financial life over the next 30 years? Is your advice fully independent (whole of market)? Can you confirm in writing exactly what I'm paying and what that covers? If you can't get clear answers to all three, it's worth having a conversation with us. We're happy to do a no-obligation review — not to tell you to switch, but to help you assess whether your current arrangement is working as well as it could.
What financial planning covers
What does a WealthPlan™ actually cover?
Your full balance sheet, a lifetime cashflow model, retirement income strategy, tax planning (ISAs, pensions, CGT, IHT), investment recommendations, protection gap analysis, estate planning, and a prioritised written action list. It's not a generic template — it's built around your specific situation, your goals from the Grab Life Wheel exercise, and the scenarios you want to stress-test. See the full WealthPlan™ process →
Do you manage investments as well as give advice?
Yes. Investment management is included within our ongoing annual fee — there's no separate charge for this. We don't charge a percentage of assets for investment management, which is one of the ways our fixed fee model creates better alignment. We use evidence-based investment approaches with low underlying fund costs, and your portfolio is managed in line with your WealthPlan™ strategy.
Do you help with mortgage advice?
Mortgage advice falls outside our core scope, but we can refer you to specialist mortgage advisers within our professional network. Property decisions — whether to buy, remortgage, downsize, or release equity — absolutely feature in your WealthPlan™ from a strategic perspective. We'll model the impact of different property decisions on your overall financial plan.
Can you help with estate planning and inheritance tax?
Yes — IHT and estate planning is a core part of what we do, particularly for clients who have accumulated significant wealth or who own property. We'll model your estate value, identify IHT exposure, and recommend strategies — gifting, trust structures, pension planning, life insurance — to manage it. For complex estate matters requiring trust documentation or legal advice, we work alongside your solicitor.
Retirement planning
When should I start planning for retirement?
The honest answer: the earlier the better, because compounding works over long timeframes. But many of our most valuable client relationships start when people are in their 40s or 50s — close enough to retirement to make the planning feel urgent, but far enough away to make real changes. Even if you're 10 or 15 years from retirement, the decisions you make now will have a significant impact on the income and flexibility you have then.
How much money do I need to retire?
It depends entirely on the life you want to live. Our WealthPlan™ process starts by getting clear on what that looks like — not in financial terms, but in human terms. What does your ideal week in retirement look like? What would you spend? Where would you live? What does long-term care provision look like for you? Once we know that, we can model the number with reasonable precision. The number most people need is different from what they assume.

WealthPlan™ · FAQs

Everything you want to know
before you start.

Common questions about the WealthPlan™ process — what it involves, what it costs, and what happens afterwards.

The WealthPlan™ process
What exactly is a WealthPlan™?
A WealthPlan™ is a written financial strategy built around your specific life — your goals, your family, your assets, and the future you want to build. It includes a full balance sheet, lifetime cashflow modelling using Voyant, tax planning, investment strategy, protection recommendations, estate planning, and a prioritised action list. It typically takes 6–8 weeks from your first meeting to receive the written document. Read the full process →
How long does the WealthPlan™ process take?
Four meetings over roughly 6–8 weeks: an initial conversation, a discovery meeting (including the Grab Life Wheel), a strategy session where we build and test your cashflow model together, and a final meeting where we walk you through the written WealthPlan™ document. Most clients say the strategy session is the most valuable — it's where the model comes to life and the abstract becomes concrete.
What is the Grab Life Wheel?
The Grab Life Wheel is a structured life exercise — not a financial one — that sits at the heart of the WealthPlan™ discovery process. We ask you to identify the areas of life that matter most to you, score your current satisfaction in each, and describe what a nine or ten out of ten would look like. For couples, both partners complete it independently. The conversation that follows is often one of the most illuminating — and useful — that clients have had. Try the Grab Life Wheel →
What happens after the WealthPlan™ is delivered?
You're under no obligation to continue working with us. If you do, we'll move into implementation — opening accounts, restructuring existing arrangements, putting agreed investment and tax strategies in place — and then into ongoing annual service. If you don't, you leave with a complete financial plan you can act on yourself or take to another adviser. The plan is yours regardless.
Fees and costs
How much does a WealthPlan™ cost?
£2,495 including VAT for most clients. For more complex situations — multiple businesses, significant property portfolios, cross-border planning — the fee may be higher and will be confirmed before you proceed. If you go on to implement recommendations with Xentum, the WealthPlan™ fee is credited against your implementation cost. Use the pricing calculator →
Is the initial meeting really free?
Yes — completely. There's no charge for the initial conversation, no paperwork to sign, and no obligation to proceed. It's a chance for both sides to decide whether we're a good fit. If we're not the right option for you, we'll say so and suggest alternatives.
What does the ongoing service cost?
Our ongoing annual fee is fixed and based on the complexity of your situation — not the size of your portfolio. It starts from £3,000 per year and includes investment management, annual reviews, ongoing tax planning, and all-year access to your adviser. There are no separate charges for the things most advisers charge separately for — fund switches, top-ups, or withdrawals from existing accounts. The full fee schedule is in our pricing calculator.
Practicalities
Where are you based and do you meet clients in person?
We're based at Mosswood, Knutsford, Cheshire. We work with clients across the UK and are flexible about how we meet — in person at our office, online via video call, or by phone. Many of our clients are based outside the North West. Distance has never been a barrier to the quality of the planning relationship.
How long does the ongoing relationship typically last?
Most of our client relationships are long-term — many spanning a decade or more. Financial planning is not a one-off transaction; it's an ongoing process of keeping your plan relevant as your life changes. The clients who get the most from the relationship are those who treat it as a genuine long-term partnership, not an annual admin exercise.
Are you regulated?
Yes. Xentum Limited is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA reference 912036). You can verify this at register.fca.org.uk. We hold CII Corporate Chartered Financial Planner status — awarded to fewer than 15% of UK advice firms — and are fully independent, meaning we recommend from the whole market rather than a restricted panel of products.
